titleEn: Braised Green Beans in Olive Oil & Tomatoes
description: A cornerstone of Aegean summer dining: tender flat green beans braised gently with sweet onions, vine-ripened tomatoes, a touch of sugar, and aromatic extra virgin olive oil, traditionally allowed to rest and served at room temperature.

ingredients.name: Flat Green Beans (Romano Beans)
ingredients.substitute: Italian flat beans from Whole Foods/Trader Joe's, or standard fresh string beans trimmed and halved lengthwise

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: High-quality cold-pressed Mediterranean EVOO (e.g., California Olive Ranch or Greek EVOO)

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Sweet Vidalia or Spanish yellow onion, thinly sliced into crescents

ingredients.name: Garlic Cloves
ingredients.substitute: Fresh garlic cloves, thinly sliced

ingredients.name: Ripe Tomatoes
ingredients.substitute: Grated Roma tomatoes, or 1 cup canned San Marzano crushed tomatoes

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Raw cane sugar or honey to balance acidity

ingredients.name: Sea Salt
ingredients.substitute: Kosher salt or fine sea salt

ingredients.name: Warm Water
ingredients.substitute: Filtered tap water or light vegetable broth

steps.instruction: Trim the stem ends of the green beans. Snap or slice them in half lengthwise if broad. Thinly slice the onions into half-moons and grate the fresh tomatoes.
In a wide, shallow heavy-bottomed pot, heat half of the olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and garlic, sautéing gently until translucent and fragrant without browning.
Layer the trimmed green beans evenly over the softened onions. Pour the grated tomatoes, salt, sugar, warm water, and the remaining olive oil evenly across the beans. Do not stir vigorously.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer undisturbed until the beans are tender and have absorbed the savory tomato juices.
Turn off the heat and let the dish cool to room temperature completely inside the covered pot. Transfer to a serving platter and chill before serving with crusty bread.

titleEn: Stuffed Grape Leaves with Herbed Rice & Pine Nuts
description: The crown jewel of the Turkish cold meze table: tender grapevine leaves rolled into slender parcels filled with aromatic short-grain rice, caramelized onions, pine nuts, sweet currants, fragrant allspice, and fresh mint, simmered in olive oil and lemon broth.

ingredients.name: Grape Leaves in Brine
ingredients.substitute: Jarred Krinos or Orlando grape leaves (available at Whole Foods, Sprouts, or international aisles), soaked in warm water to desalt

ingredients.name: Turkish Short-Grain Rice (Baldo)
ingredients.substitute: Arborio rice, Calrose medium-grain rice, or Spanish bomba rice

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Robust cold-pressed Mediterranean extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onions
ingredients.substitute: Finely minced yellow onions (generous onion amount is essential for sweetness)

ingredients.name: Pine Nuts
ingredients.substitute: Raw Mediterranean pine nuts or finely chopped slivered almonds

ingredients.name: Dried Currants
ingredients.substitute: Zante currants or finely chopped Thompson seedless raisins

ingredients.name: Ground Allspice & Cinnamon
ingredients.substitute: 3/4 tsp ground allspice plus 1/4 tsp ground Ceylon cinnamon

ingredients.name: Dried Spearmint
ingredients.substitute: Dried crushed mint leaves or 2 tbsp finely minced fresh mint

ingredients.name: Fresh Dill & Flat-Leaf Parsley
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped fresh supermarket dill and Italian parsley

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed lemon juice plus 1 sliced lemon for layering

ingredients.name: Warm Water
ingredients.substitute: Warm filtered water

steps.instruction: Unroll the jarred grape leaves and soak them in a large bowl of boiling water for 10 minutes to remove excess salt and soften veins. Drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Heat 1/4 cup olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Toast pine nuts until pale golden (2 mins), then add finely minced onions and sauté until deeply softened and glossy.

Stir in washed rice, currants, allspice, cinnamon, dried mint, salt, and 1/2 cup warm water. Cover and simmer over low heat until liquid is absorbed (the rice will remain par-cooked). Off heat, fold in chopped fresh dill and parsley, then cool.

Lay a grape leaf flat on a clean board with the vein side up and stem snipped. Place 1 teaspoon of filling near the stem end. Fold sides inward and roll tightly into a slender cylinder the thickness of a small finger.

Line the bottom of a wide pot with torn or damaged grape leaves. Arrange rolled sarmas seam-side down in tight, neat concentric circles. Top with lemon slices, remaining olive oil, 3/4 cup warm water, and invert a heatproof ceramic plate on top to keep them submerged.
Cover pot with lid, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest simmer and cook gently until leaves are tender and rice is cooked through.
Allow sarmas to cool completely inside the pot at room temperature before transferring to a platter. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving with lemon wedges.

titleEn: Braised Stuffed Eggplants with Caramelized Onions & Tomatoes
description: Literally translating to 'the imam fainted' with pleasure at the generous use of olive oil: tender whole eggplants roasted and stuffed with a meltingly rich filling of caramelized onions, garlic, ripe tomatoes, and fresh Italian parsley.

ingredients.name: Italian or Japanese Eggplants
ingredients.substitute: Medium slender Italian eggplants or Japanese/Chinese eggplants (avoid large fibrous globe eggplants)

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: High-grade Spanish, Greek, or California extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onions
ingredients.substitute: Sweet onions (such as Vidalia or Walla Walla), thinly sliced into half-moons

ingredients.name: Garlic Cloves
ingredients.substitute: Fresh whole garlic cloves, peeled and thickly sliced

ingredients.name: Ripe Plum Tomatoes
ingredients.substitute: Diced fresh Roma tomatoes or drained canned petite diced tomatoes

ingredients.name: Green Cubanelle Peppers
ingredients.substitute: Cubanelle peppers, Italian sweet frying peppers, or 1 green bell pepper sliced into strips

ingredients.name: Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped fresh Italian flat-leaf parsley

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Granulated sugar

ingredients.name: Sea Salt & Black Pepper
ingredients.substitute: Fine sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper

steps.instruction: Peel lengthwise strips of skin from each eggplant to create a zebra pattern. Make a deep lengthwise slit down the center of each, leaving 1/2-inch intact at the top and bottom. Soak in salted water for 15 minutes to reduce bitterness, then pat thoroughly dry.
Brush eggplants generously with 3 tablespoons olive oil. Roast on a parchment-lined baking sheet at 400°F (200°C) until tender and golden, turning once halfway through.

In a wide skillet, heat remaining olive oil over medium-low heat. Sauté sliced onions and peppers with a pinch of salt until caramelized and sweet. Add sliced garlic and cook 2 minutes more. Stir in tomatoes, sugar, and black pepper, cooking until tomatoes soften. Fold in fresh parsley.

Transfer roasted eggplants to a wide baking dish or shallow braising pot. Gently widen the central cavity of each eggplant with two forks. Spoon generous mounds of warm onion-tomato filling into each pocket.
Pour 1/3 cup warm water around the eggplants. Cover pot or pan with foil and braise on low stovetop heat or in a 350°F (175°C) oven until meltingly silky.
Allow to cool to room temperature in the pan before serving. Garnish with extra fresh parsley leaves and a squeeze of fresh lemon.

titleEn: Braised Artichoke Bottoms Filled with Spring Vegetables & Dill
description: An Aegean culinary hallmark of elegance: whole fresh artichoke cups gently braised in fresh orange and lemon juices with extra virgin olive oil, crowned with tender sweet peas, diced carrots, and fragrant fresh dill.

ingredients.name: Artichoke Bottoms (Enginar Çanağı)
ingredients.substitute: Frozen artichoke bottoms (found at Trader Joe's or Mediterranean markets), thawed, or trimmed fresh globe artichoke hearts kept in acidulated lemon water

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Fruity Greek or Turkish extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Baby Carrots
ingredients.substitute: Carrots peeled and finely diced into 1/4-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Sweet Green Peas
ingredients.substitute: Frozen sweet petite peas (thawed) or fresh shelled English peas

ingredients.name: Fresh Orange Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed orange juice (provides quintessential Aegean citrus sweetness)

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed lemon juice

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.substitute: Unbleached all-purpose flour or cornstarch for a silky glaze

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: White granulated sugar

ingredients.name: Fresh Dill
ingredients.substitute: Fresh dill, finely chopped (essential Turkish seasoning for artichoke)

ingredients.name: Sea Salt
ingredients.substitute: Fine sea salt

steps.instruction: In a small bowl, whisk together fresh orange juice, lemon juice, flour, sugar, salt, and olive oil to create an emulsion.

Arrange the artichoke bottoms cup-side up in a single layer in a wide shallow saucepan. Fill the hollow center of each cup generously with diced carrots and sweet peas, scattering any leftover vegetables around them.
Pour the citrus-olive oil emulsion evenly over the artichoke cups and vegetables. Add 1/4 cup warm water around the edges.
Cover with a tight lid, bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then turn to low and braise until the artichokes and carrots are fork-tender and the sauce has reduced to a glistening glaze.

Turn off heat, stir in half of the chopped fresh dill, and allow the artichokes to cool completely in the covered pan to absorb all flavors. Chill for at least 1 hour, garnish with remaining dill, and serve cold.

titleEn: Crispy Pan-Fried Zucchini & Herb Fritters
description: Golden-crusted, tender-centered zucchini fritters packed with fresh dill, mint, scallions, and creamy sheep's milk feta cheese, served hot or at room temperature alongside cool garlic yogurt sauce.

ingredients.name: Medium Zucchini
ingredients.substitute: Standard green zucchini or light green Italian cousa squash

ingredients.name: Crumbled Turkish White Cheese or Greek Feta
ingredients.substitute: Block Greek feta cheese packed in brine, crumbled (avoid pre-crumbled dry feta)

ingredients.name: Large Eggs
ingredients.substitute: Standard organic large eggs, beaten

ingredients.name: Scallions (Green Onions)
ingredients.substitute: Scallions, green and pale white parts finely sliced

ingredients.name: Fresh Dill
ingredients.substitute: Fresh dill, finely minced

ingredients.name: Fresh Spearmint
ingredients.substitute: Fresh mint or 1 tsp dried spearmint

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.substitute: All-purpose flour or 1:1 gluten-free baking flour

ingredients.name: Baking Powder
ingredients.substitute: Standard baking powder for fluffiness

ingredients.name: Olive Oil (or high-heat cooking oil for frying)
ingredients.substitute: Light olive oil, avocado oil, or sunflower oil

ingredients.name: Plain Whole Milk Greek Yogurt
ingredients.substitute: Plain whole milk Greek yogurt (e.g., Fage 5%) mixed with 1 grated garlic clove and pinch of salt for dipping

steps.instruction: Coarsely grate the zucchini. Toss with 1/2 tsp salt in a colander and let drain for 15 minutes. Using your hands or a clean kitchen towel, squeeze out as much moisture as physically possible; dry zucchini is crucial for crispy fritters.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs. Stir in the drained zucchini, crumbled feta, sliced scallions, chopped dill, mint, baking powder, and a generous pinch of black pepper.
Sprinkle the flour over the mixture and fold together just until a cohesive batter forms. Do not overmix.

Heat 1/4 inch of oil in a wide heavy non-stick or cast-iron skillet over medium heat until shimmering (350°F / 175°C). Drop heaping tablespoons of batter into the pan, flattening slightly with the back of the spoon.
Fry in batches without overcrowding for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden brown and crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain.
Serve warm or at room temperature with cool garlicky Greek yogurt on the side.

titleEn: Cranberry Beans Stewed with Carrots, Potatoes & Garlic
description: An indispensable Turkish meze tavern classic: creamy speckled borlotti (cranberry) beans stewed slowly with diced carrots, potatoes, sweet onions, whole garlic cloves, tomato paste, and fruity olive oil, garnished with fresh flat-leaf parsley and lemon.

ingredients.name: Fresh or Dried Borlotti / Cranberry Beans
ingredients.substitute: Fresh or dried cranberry beans, or two 15-oz cans of Roman/cannellini/pinto beans rinsed and drained

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Cold-pressed Mediterranean extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Finely diced yellow onion

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.substitute: Peeled and sliced into 1/4-inch coins or half-moons

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold Potato
ingredients.substitute: Peeled and diced into 1/2-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Garlic Cloves
ingredients.substitute: Whole garlic cloves, peeled and halved

ingredients.name: Tomato Paste
ingredients.substitute: Double-concentrated tomato paste (e.g., Mutti)

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: White granulated sugar

ingredients.name: Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped Italian parsley

ingredients.name: Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Fresh lemon juice

steps.instruction: If using dried beans, soak overnight and boil in water for 25 minutes until partially tender; drain. (If using canned beans, rinse well; cooking time will be reduced by 15 minutes).
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Add diced onions, sliced carrots, and garlic cloves; cook until onions soften and carrots are coated in oil.
Stir in tomato paste and sugar, cooking for 1 minute until paste releases its sweet aroma. Add diced potato and par-cooked beans.

Pour in 2 cups of boiling water and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and braise until beans, potatoes, and carrots are meltingly tender and the liquid forms a thick, rich broth.
Stir in lemon juice. Remove from heat and allow to cool completely in the pot. Serve at room temperature or chilled, adorned with abundant chopped fresh parsley.

titleEn: Braised Celery Root with Orange Juice & Carrots
description: A refined Ottoman winter classic: earthy celery root (celeriac) peeled and cubed, braised gently with sweet carrots in fresh orange juice, lemon, and rich olive oil until tender and glistening, topped with its aromatic tender green leaves.

ingredients.name: Celery Root (Celeriac / Kereviz)
ingredients.substitute: Large fresh celery root from Whole Foods, Sprouts, or conventional grocers; thick fibrous skin trimmed off and flesh cubed

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.substitute: Peeled and sliced into diagonal 1/2-inch chunks

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped yellow onion

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Fresh Orange Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed Valencia or Navel orange juice

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed lemon juice

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Granulated sugar

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.substitute: All-purpose flour dissolved in the juice for a velvety sauce

ingredients.name: Tender Celery Leaves or Fresh Dill
ingredients.substitute: Coarsely chopped celery leaves from the inner heart of a celery stalk, or fresh dill

steps.instruction: Peel the knobby exterior off the celery root with a sturdy chef's knife. Cut the white flesh into 1-inch cubes and place immediately in a bowl of cold water with a squeeze of lemon juice to prevent discoloration.
In a wide shallow pot, warm the olive oil over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion until translucent and fragrant.
Add sliced carrots and drained celery root cubes. Stir to coat thoroughly in the warm olive oil for 2 minutes.
Whisk orange juice, lemon juice, flour, sugar, and salt together. Pour over the vegetables. Add 1/4 cup water if needed so liquid reaches halfway up the vegetables.
Bring to a boil, then cover tightly, reduce heat to low, and braise until the celery root and carrots are knife-tender.
Sprinkle chopped celery leaves or dill on top. Let cool completely in the pot to room temperature before serving.

titleEn: Fried Eggplant & Peppers in Rich Garlic Tomato Sauce
description: An authentic Turkish summer meze staple (unrelated to North African shakshuka): crispy fried cubes of eggplant, zucchini, and sweet green peppers blanketed in a simmered garlicky tomato and red pepper sauce, served cold with thick yogurt.

ingredients.name: Eggplants
ingredients.substitute: Italian or globe eggplants, peeled in zebra stripes and cut into 3/4-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Zucchini
ingredients.substitute: Green zucchini cut into 3/4-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Cubanelle or Italian Sweet Peppers
ingredients.substitute: Cubanelle peppers, shishito peppers, or 1 green bell pepper seeded and cut into bite-sized chunks

ingredients.name: Ripe Roma Tomatoes
ingredients.substitute: Grated fresh Roma tomatoes or 1.5 cups canned crushed tomatoes

ingredients.name: Garlic Cloves
ingredients.substitute: Finely minced fresh garlic

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil for the tomato sauce

ingredients.name: Frying Oil (Sunflower or Olive Oil)
ingredients.substitute: Sunflower, canola, or light olive oil for shallow-frying

ingredients.name: Red Wine Vinegar or Apple Cider Vinegar
ingredients.substitute: Red wine vinegar (adds traditional Aegean tang)

ingredients.name: Sugar, Salt & Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: 1/2 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper / Maras pepper flakes

steps.instruction: Toss eggplant cubes with 1 tsp salt in a colander and let rest for 20 minutes to draw out bitter liquids. Press dry thoroughly with paper towels.

Heat 1 cup frying oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat (365°F / 185°C). Fry eggplant cubes in batches until deep golden and tender (4-5 mins). Drain on paper towels. Quickly fry zucchini and peppers (2-3 mins); drain alongside eggplant.
In a separate saucepan, heat 3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add grated tomatoes, vinegar, sugar, salt, and red pepper flakes. Simmer on medium-low heat until the sauce thickens into a glossy, rich condiment.

Arrange the fried vegetables on a wide shallow serving dish. Pour the warm garlic tomato sauce evenly over the top. Allow to rest until it reaches room temperature, allowing the vegetables to soak up the sauce.

titleEn: Braised Leeks with Sweet Carrots & Rice in Olive Oil
description: A nourishing staple of Turkish home cooking: thick-cut leeks braised gently with sweet carrots, a sprinkle of rice, freshly squeezed lemon juice, and luscious olive oil until melt-in-your-mouth tender.

ingredients.name: Fresh Leeks
ingredients.substitute: 3 large leeks, dark green tops trimmed, washed thoroughly to remove grit, and sliced diagonally into 1.5-inch cylinders

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.substitute: Peeled and cut diagonally into 1/2-inch coins to match the leeks

ingredients.name: Short-Grain White Rice
ingredients.substitute: Baldo, Arborio, or Calrose medium-grain white rice rinsed

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: High-quality extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed lemon juice (vital for balancing the leeks' sweetness)

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Granulated sugar

ingredients.name: Sea Salt
ingredients.substitute: Fine sea salt

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.substitute: Warm filtered water or light vegetable broth

steps.instruction: Clean leeks thoroughly under cold running water to eliminate trapped dirt. Slice diagonally into 1.5-inch pieces. Slice carrots diagonally.
In a wide shallow saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced carrots and sauté for 3 minutes to infuse the oil with orange color and sweetness.
Add the sliced leeks, turning them gently in the oil for 2 minutes. Sprinkle the washed rice evenly across the vegetables.
Pour in 1 cup warm water, lemon juice, sugar, and salt. Do not stir, allowing the rice to settle on top.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with a tight lid, and simmer gently until the leeks are buttery soft and the rice is swollen and tender.
Turn off heat and let rest undisturbed until room temperature. Serve with lemon slices and crusty sourdough bread.

titleEn: Olive Oil Braised Bell Peppers Stuffed with Spiced Rice
description: Vibrant bell peppers stuffed with a fragrant Ottoman pilaf filling of short-grain rice, caramelized onions, pine nuts, dried currants, cinnamon, mint, and fresh dill, gently braised in an olive oil broth and served cold.

ingredients.name: Medium Bell Peppers (Green, Yellow, or Red)
ingredients.substitute: Standard medium bell peppers or Turkish Dolmalık Biber (small thin-skinned green peppers)

ingredients.name: Short-Grain Rice (Baldo)
ingredients.substitute: Arborio or Calrose rice, rinsed until water runs clear

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onions
ingredients.substitute: Finely minced yellow onions

ingredients.name: Pine Nuts
ingredients.substitute: Raw pine nuts

ingredients.name: Dried Zante Currants
ingredients.substitute: Dried currants or finely minced black raisins

ingredients.name: Ground Allspice, Cinnamon & Mint
ingredients.substitute: 1 tsp dried mint, 1/2 tsp allspice, and 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon

ingredients.name: Fresh Dill & Flat-Leaf Parsley
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped fresh dill and Italian parsley

ingredients.name: Tomatoes for Capping
ingredients.substitute: Fresh round tomatoes, cut into wedges or rounds to cap each stuffed pepper

steps.instruction: Slice the tops off the bell peppers and scoop out seeds and membranes. Reserve pepper bodies. Slice tomatoes into disks to use as lids.
In a skillet, heat 1/4 cup olive oil over medium heat. Toast pine nuts for 2 minutes, then sauté minced onions until soft and translucent.

Stir in rice, currants, allspice, cinnamon, dried mint, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 cup warm water. Cook covered on low until water is absorbed (rice will be half-cooked). Stir in chopped dill and parsley; cool slightly.
Fill each pepper loosely to 3/4 capacity with the rice mixture (allowing room for rice to expand). Cap each pepper securely with a slice of fresh tomato.
Stand the stuffed peppers upright snugly in a deep pot. Drizzle the remaining 1/4 cup olive oil over the peppers and pour 1.5 cups boiling water into the base of the pot.
Cover with a tight lid, bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat until pepper skins are tender and rice is thoroughly cooked.
Cool in the pot to room temperature before plating. Chill in refrigerator and serve cold.

titleEn: Fresh Broad Beans Braised in Olive Oil with Dill & Garlic Yogurt
description: An iconic Turkish spring specialty: whole tender young broad (fava) beans in their pods, braised with olive oil, lemon, a flour slurry, and a mountain of fresh dill, traditionally crowned with thick garlic yogurt.

ingredients.name: Fresh Young Broad Beans in Pods (Fava Beans)
ingredients.substitute: Fresh whole baby fava bean pods (found at Middle Eastern/farmers markets), or frozen baby fava beans (Bakla), or fresh Romano flat green beans

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: High-quality extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Finely diced yellow onion

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.substitute: All-purpose flour (whisked with water & lemon to keep beans pale and sauce silky)

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Fresh lemon juice

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Granulated sugar

ingredients.name: Fresh Dill
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped fresh dill (an indispensable pairing for bakla)

ingredients.name: Whole Milk Greek Yogurt & Garlic
ingredients.substitute: Whole milk Greek yogurt whisked with 1 crushed garlic clove and pinch of salt

steps.instruction: Trim the stringy edges and tips of the broad bean pods, snapping each pod into 2 or 3 bite-sized pieces. Drop immediately into cold water mixed with 1 tbsp flour and lemon juice to prevent blackening.
In a wide saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion until soft and translucent.
Drain the broad beans and add them to the saucepan. Sauté for 3 minutes until coated in olive oil.
Whisk 1 tbsp flour, 2 tbsp lemon juice, sugar, 1 tsp salt, and 1 cup warm water until completely smooth. Pour over the beans.
Bring to a boil, cover tightly, and simmer on low heat until the beans are completely tender and the sauce has emulsified.
Fold in half the fresh dill. Let cool completely in the pot. Serve at room temperature topped with a generous dollop of garlicky Greek yogurt and remaining dill.

titleEn: Delicate Stuffed Zucchini Blossoms with Herbed Rice
description: An Aegean treasure from coastal Bodrum and Ayvalık: tender yellow zucchini blossoms stuffed with sweet caramelized onions, short-grain rice, fresh mint, dill, and olive oil, gently steamed and served chilled.

ingredients.name: Fresh Zucchini Blossoms (Squash Flowers)
ingredients.substitute: Fresh male or female squash blossoms (available in summer at Whole Foods, farmers markets, or Italian grocers); alternatively, baby sweet snacking peppers with tops removed

ingredients.name: Turkish Short-Grain Rice (Baldo)
ingredients.substitute: Arborio or Calrose rice, rinsed

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Delicate, fruity extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Very finely grated or minced yellow onion

ingredients.name: Ripe Tomato
ingredients.substitute: Grated fresh tomato

ingredients.name: Fresh Spearmint & Dill
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped fresh mint and fresh dill

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar & Sea Salt
ingredients.substitute: 1/2 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp fine sea salt, and a pinch of black pepper

ingredients.name: Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Fresh lemon juice

steps.instruction: Carefully open the flower petals of each blossom and snip off the inner pistil/stamen without tearing the delicate petals. Rinse gently under cold water and let drain on paper towels.
In a bowl, mix rinsed rice, grated onion, grated tomato, chopped mint, chopped dill, half the olive oil, sugar, salt, and pepper into a fragrant raw filling.
Using a teaspoon, gently spoon about 1.5 teaspoons of filling into the center of each blossom (do not overfill, as rice swells). Fold the petal tips over one another to seal the opening.
Arrange the stuffed blossoms seam-side down in snug concentric circles in a wide pot. Drizzle remaining olive oil and lemon juice over top, and add 3/4 cup warm water around them.
Place an inverted heat-proof plate over the flowers to prevent them from opening. Cover pot, bring to a boil, then cook over low heat for 25 minutes until rice is fully cooked and tender.
Cool in the pot completely, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Serve chilled with lemon wedges.

titleEn: Spiced Red Lentil & Bulgur Finger Patties with Herbs
description: A beloved Turkish vegan culinary classic: pureed tender red lentils steamed with fine bulgur, kneaded with sautéed onions, tomato and pepper pastes, ground cumin, scallions, parsley, and pomegranate molasses, squeezed into bite-sized finger-marked patties.

ingredients.name: Red Lentils (Kırmızı Mercimek)
ingredients.substitute: Split red lentils (available at Trader Joe's, Whole Foods, or any supermarket)

ingredients.name: Fine Grind Bulgur (#1 Köftelik Bulgur)
ingredients.substitute: Fine #1 bulgur wheat (such as Sunnyland Mills or Sadaf), or whole-wheat couscous if fine bulgur is unavailable

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Finely minced yellow onion

ingredients.name: Tomato Paste
ingredients.substitute: Double-concentrated tomato paste

ingredients.name: Turkish Red Pepper Paste (Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: Mild red pepper paste (Tat / Öncü), or 1 tbsp tomato paste mixed with 1 tsp smoked sweet paprika and pinch of cayenne

ingredients.name: Pomegranate Molasses (Nar Ekşisi)
ingredients.substitute: 100% pure pomegranate molasses (Cortas or Al Wadi) or 1.5 tbsp fresh lemon juice plus 1/2 tsp balsamic glaze

ingredients.name: Ground Cumin & Aleppo Pepper (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: 1 tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes or Aleppo pepper

ingredients.name: Scallions & Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley
ingredients.substitute: 5 thinly sliced scallions and 1/2 bunch finely minced Italian parsley

ingredients.name: Crisp Romaine Lettuce Leaves
ingredients.substitute: Washed and crisped romaine lettuce leaves for serving

steps.instruction: In a pot, combine rinsed red lentils with 3 cups of water. Bring to a boil, skim foam, reduce heat, and simmer until lentils are completely broken down into a soft puree.

Turn off heat while the lentils are still slightly soupy. Stir in the fine bulgur thoroughly. Cover tightly with a lid and let sit for 15 minutes; the bulgur will absorb the remaining hot liquid and steam to perfection.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté the finely minced onion until golden. Add tomato paste and pepper paste, sautéing for 2 minutes to caramelize.

Transfer the warm lentil-bulgur mixture to a wide shallow bowl or kneading tray. Pour in the hot onion-paste mixture, cumin, pepper flakes, pomegranate molasses, and 1.5 tsp salt. Knead by hand until smooth, cohesive, and cool enough to handle.
Fold in the sliced scallions and chopped fresh parsley, kneading gently until evenly distributed.
Grab walnut-sized portions of the warm mixture in the palm of your hand and squeeze firmly with your fingers to form elongated patties with distinct finger impressions.
Arrange on a platter lined with crisp romaine lettuce leaves and lemon wedges. Serve at room temperature.

titleEn: Braised Baby Okra with Tomatoes, Olive Oil & Lemon
description: A celebrated Aegean summer dish: tender petite baby okra trimmed carefully into conical hats, braised in golden olive oil with grated sweet tomatoes, onions, garlic, and fresh lemon juice to achieve a silky, completely slime-free texture.

ingredients.name: Fresh or Frozen Baby Okra
ingredients.substitute: Fresh small young okra (under 2 inches) or frozen whole baby okra (found at Middle Eastern, Indian, or Whole Foods grocers)

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Finely diced yellow onion

ingredients.name: Garlic Cloves
ingredients.substitute: Thinly sliced garlic cloves

ingredients.name: Ripe Tomatoes
ingredients.substitute: Fresh peeled and grated tomatoes or 1.25 cups canned crushed tomatoes

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed lemon juice (acid prevents okra from becoming mucilaginous)

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Granulated sugar

ingredients.name: Sea Salt
ingredients.substitute: Fine sea salt

steps.instruction: Carefully trim the woody stem of each fresh okra pod with a small paring knife, carving around the crown in a conical spiral pencil-sharpener motion without cutting into the inner seed pod (cutting the pod releases mucilage). Soak trimmed okra in cold water with 2 tbsp lemon juice for 15 minutes, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pot over medium heat. Sauté diced onions and sliced garlic until translucent and fragrant.
Add the grated tomatoes, sugar, salt, and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the tomato sauce is slightly reduced and rich.
Gently add the drained okra to the pan in an even layer. Pour 1/2 cup warm water around the edges. Do not stir with a spoon; gently shake the pan by the handles to distribute the sauce.
Cover with a tight lid, bring to a simmer, and cook over low heat undisturbed until okra is tender but holds its shape.
Remove from heat and allow to cool completely in the pot. Serve at room temperature or chilled with lemon wedges.

titleEn: Braised Jerusalem Artichokes with Carrots & Lemon in Olive Oil
description: A delicate and nutty winter root vegetable specialty: Jerusalem artichokes (sunchokes) braised with sweet carrots, a handful of rice, fresh lemon juice, and extra virgin olive oil, finished with vibrant fresh dill.

ingredients.name: Jerusalem Artichokes (Sunchokes / Yer Elması)
ingredients.substitute: Fresh sunchokes / Jerusalem artichokes (available in the root vegetable section of Whole Foods, Sprouts, or Wegmans), peeled and sliced into 1/2-inch rounds

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.substitute: Peeled and sliced into 1/3-inch coins

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped yellow onion

ingredients.name: Short-Grain White Rice
ingredients.substitute: Baldo, Arborio, or Calrose medium-grain white rice rinsed

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.substitute: Cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
ingredients.substitute: Freshly squeezed lemon juice

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Granulated sugar

ingredients.name: Sea Salt
ingredients.substitute: Fine sea salt

ingredients.name: Fresh Dill
ingredients.substitute: Finely chopped fresh dill

steps.instruction: Peel the knobby sunchokes with a vegetable peeler or paring knife. Slice into 1/2-inch thick coins and place immediately into a bowl of water with 1 tbsp lemon juice to keep them bright.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow saucepan over medium heat. Sauté the diced onion and carrot slices for 4 minutes until the carrots begin to glisten.
Drain the sunchoke slices and add them to the pot with the rinsed rice. Gently turn to coat in olive oil.
Pour in 1 cup warm water, remaining lemon juice, sugar, and salt. Bring to a gentle boil.
Cover with a tight lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer until sunchokes are tender and creamy when pierced with a fork (approx. 20-25 minutes). Do not overcook as sunchokes soften quickly.
Turn off heat, stir in half the chopped fresh dill, and let cool completely in the pot. Serve at room temperature garnished with remaining fresh dill and extra virgin olive oil drizzle.

titleEn: Sun-Dried Eggplants Stuffed with Spiced Rice and Sumac
description: Gaziantep crown jewel of rehydrated sun-dried eggplant skins stuffed with aromatic short-grain rice, sweet onions, sumac, pomegranate molasses, and mint, braised slowly in fragrant olive oil.

ingredients.name: Sun-Dried Hollow Eggplants (Kuru Patlıcan)
ingredients.substitute: Dried baby eggplants or dried bell peppers

ingredients.name: Baldo or Calrose Rice (washed)
ingredients.substitute: Short-grain sushi or risotto rice

steps.instruction: Boil dried eggplants in salted water for 8-10 minutes until soft and pliable; drain and rinse in cold water.
Mix raw rice with diced onions, garlic, tomato paste, pepper paste, pomegranate molasses, sumac, mint, salt, and half the olive oil.
Stuff eggplants halfway (rice will expand) and pinch mouths closed. Arrange snugly mouth-to-bottom in a heavy pot.
Weight with a heatproof plate, pour 2 cups warm water and remaining olive oil over, and simmer covered on low heat until tender.

titleEn: Ottoman Braised Zucchini with Ground Meat or Onion Herb Jam (Kabak Kalye)
description: Historical Ottoman palace olive oil dish of thick zucchini rounds braised with sweet caramelized onions, sour grapes or lemon juice, fresh mint, and fragrant dill.

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice & Sugar
ingredients.substitute: Verjuice (koruk suyu)

steps.instruction: Caramelize sliced onions in olive oil in a wide shallow pan until sweet and tender.
Layer zucchini rounds over the onions, seasoning each layer with salt, sugar, and black pepper.
Add lemon juice and 1/2 cup water. Cover and simmer gently until zucchinis are tender yet intact.
Sprinkle with copious fresh dill and mint; cool to room temperature before serving.

titleEn: Black Sea Green Bean and Rice Stew (Fasulye Diblesi)
description: Beloved Giresun and Black Sea home recipe: tender flat green beans layered with short-grain rice, sweet onions, and ripe tomatoes, slowly stewed together in virgin olive oil.

ingredients.name: Flat Green Romano Beans (cut into 1 cm pieces)
ingredients.substitute: Stringless Italian flat beans

ingredients.name: Baldo Rice (rinsed)
ingredients.substitute: Arborio or Calrose rice

steps.instruction: Layer half the chopped green beans in the bottom of a pot; top with chopped onions and washed rice.
Cover with remaining green beans and top with grated tomatoes, olive oil, salt, and sugar.
Add 1 cup hot water, cover tightly, and simmer on lowest heat undisturbed until beans and rice are tender.
Gently fold once, rest for 15 minutes, and serve warm or at room temperature.

titleEn: Aegean Black-Eyed Pea Salad with Lemon and Herbs
description: Vibrant Aegean coastal salad of tender boiled black-eyed peas tossed with sweet red peppers, scallions, fresh parsley, and sumac in an abundant dressing of early-harvest olive oil and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: Dried Black-Eyed Peas (Börülce, boiled until tender)
ingredients.substitute: Canned black-eyed peas, rinsed and drained

ingredients.name: Red Capia Pepper & Green Frying Pepper (diced)
ingredients.substitute: Red and green bell peppers

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice, Pomegranate Molasses & Sumac

steps.instruction: Boil black-eyed peas in salted water until tender but holding their shape; drain and cool.
Toss cooled peas with diced peppers, sliced scallions, chopped parsley, and dill.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, sumac, and sea salt into a dressing.
Pour dressing over salad, toss well, and let rest 15 minutes before serving.

titleEn: Braised Brussels Sprouts in Olive Oil and Orange Juice
description: Modern Turkish Aegean winter classic: fresh Brussels sprouts braised with sweet carrots, shallots, and freshly squeezed orange juice in extra virgin olive oil, served chilled with dill.

ingredients.name: Shallots or Pearl Onions
ingredients.substitute: Sliced yellow sweet onion

steps.instruction: Sauté shallots and carrots in olive oil in a wide pan for 3 minutes until glistening.
Add halved Brussels sprouts cut-side down, searing lightly for 2 minutes.
Pour in orange juice, sugar, salt, and 1/4 cup water. Simmer covered on low heat until fork-tender.
Cool in the pan with lid on to absorb olive oil glaze; serve chilled with fresh dill.

titleEn: Aegean Wild Blessed Thistle with Lemon-Egg Liaison (Şevketi Bostan)
description: Wild Aegean endemic delicacy: earthy, fibrous roots and prickly leaves of blessed thistle (şevketi bostan) braised with scallions in olive oil, bound with an egg-lemon terbiye liaison.

ingredients.name: Fresh Blessed Thistle (Şevketi Bostan, roots scrubbed & cut)
ingredients.substitute: Cardoons or artichoke stems and hearts

steps.instruction: Clean and soak thistle roots in lemon water to prevent browning.
Sauté scallions in olive oil, add drained thistle roots and leaves with 1.5 cups water, and simmer covered until tender.
Whisk egg yolk, lemon juice, and 1 tsp flour; temper with warm pot liquid and stir gently into the dish.
Simmer 2 minutes, remove from heat, scatter dill, and serve warm or at room temperature.

titleEn: Antalya Summer Tomato, Pepper and Bulgur Stew (Cive)
description: Antalya Mediterranean summer harvest dish: mountain-heaped ripe tomatoes, green and red frying peppers, and lots of garlic stewed in olive oil with coarse bulgur and fresh basil.

ingredients.name: Ripe Vine Tomatoes (peeled & chopped)
ingredients.substitute: Canned Italian plum tomatoes, crushed

ingredients.name: Green Frying Peppers & Red Capia Peppers
ingredients.substitute: Sweet Italian peppers

ingredients.name: Coarse Bulgur (Pilavlık)
ingredients.substitute: Coarse bulgur or rice

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil & Fresh Basil/Mint

steps.instruction: Sauté sliced peppers and garlic in olive oil until sweet and lightly softened.
Add chopped tomatoes, sugar, and salt; simmer until tomatoes release their juices.
Stir in coarse bulgur, cover, and simmer on gentle heat until bulgur softens and stew thickens.
Stir in torn fresh basil or mint; rest 20 minutes before serving with rustic crusty bread.

titleEn: Braised Cauliflower in Olive Oil with Carrots and Tomatoes
description: Comforting winter olive oil classic of fresh cauliflower florets, sliced sweet carrots, and onions gently braised in tomato paste and olive oil with a squeeze of fresh lemon.

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil & Lemon Juice

steps.instruction: Sauté diced onion and sliced carrots in olive oil until golden; stir in tomato paste.
Add cauliflower florets, tossing to coat in the aromatic base.
Add 1 cup hot water, lemon juice, sugar, and salt. Simmer covered on medium-low until cauliflower is tender.
Cool in the pot to room temperature, scatter parsley, and serve.

titleEn: Stuffed White Cabbage Rolls with Herbed Rice (Lahana Sarması)
description: Melt-in-the-mouth winter cabbage rolls filled with spiced rice, currants, pine nuts, onions, and cinnamon, braised slowly in olive oil and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: White Cabbage (blanched tender leaves)
ingredients.substitute: Savoy cabbage leaves

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil & Lemon Juice

steps.instruction: Blanch cabbage leaves in boiling water for 3 minutes until pliable; trim thick ribs.
Sauté onions, pine nuts, currants, spices, and rice in olive oil for 5 minutes with a splash of water to par-cook.
Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold sides, and roll into neat cigars. Pack tightly in a heavy pot.
Weight with a plate, add 1.5 cups water and olive oil, and simmer covered on low heat until tender.

titleEn: Stuffed Whole Celeriac Bulbs with Herbed Rice (Kereviz Dolması)
description: Ottoman imperial vegetarian showstopper: whole hollowed celeriac root bulbs filled with pine nut, currant, and herbed rice filling, braised in freshly squeezed orange juice and olive oil.

ingredients.name: Medium Celeriac Roots (peeled & hollowed)
ingredients.substitute: Celery roots

steps.instruction: Peel celeriac bulbs, level bases so they stand upright, and hollow out centers using a melon baller.
Sauté onions, pine nuts, currants, and rice in olive oil until fragrant.
Stuff rice filling into celeriac cavities, place in a braising pan, and pour orange juice and olive oil around.
Cover and simmer gently until celeriac bulbs are knife-tender; cool and garnish with fresh dill.

titleEn: Braised White Cabbage and Rice Stew (Kapuska)
description: Wholesome Anatolian winter braise of shredded sweet white cabbage cooked down with onions, tomato and pepper paste, rice, olive oil, and crushed red chili flakes.

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil & Lemon Juice

steps.instruction: Sauté diced onion in olive oil until golden; stir in tomato and pepper paste.
Add shredded cabbage in batches, tossing until cabbage wilts down in the pot.
Sprinkle rice over the cabbage, add 1.5 cups hot water, lemon juice, chili flakes, and salt.
Simmer covered on low heat until cabbage is tender and rice is cooked.

titleEn: Braised Pearl Onion and Wild Mushroom Ragout (Mantar Yahnisi)
description: Earthy forest mushroom stew with golden caramelized pearl onions, garlic cloves, sweet peppers, and fresh thyme slow-braised in rich olive oil and tomato juices.

ingredients.name: Button or Cremini Mushrooms (halved)
ingredients.substitute: Wild forest chanterelle or porcini mushrooms

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil & Fresh Thyme

steps.instruction: Sauté pearl onions in olive oil until golden; add sliced peppers and whole garlic cloves.
Add mushroom halves over high heat so they brown without releasing too much water.
Stir in tomato paste, diced tomatoes, fresh thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat until sauce is rich and glossy.

titleEn: Braised Fresh Green Black-Eyed Beans in Olive Oil
description: Aegean summer essential: slender fresh green cowpea pods trimmed and braised gently with ripe summer tomatoes, garlic cloves, sweet onions, and cold-pressed olive oil.

ingredients.name: Fresh Green Black-Eyed Cowpeas (Taze Börülce, trimmed & snapped in half)
ingredients.substitute: Long yard-long beans or fresh Romano green beans

steps.instruction: Sauté sliced onions and garlic in olive oil until sweet and translucent.
Add snapped fresh börülce pods and cook for 3 minutes until bright green.
Add grated tomatoes, sugar, salt, and 1/2 cup warm water. Cover and simmer gently until pods are tender.
Rest covered until completely cool; drizzle with lemon juice before serving.

titleEn: Aegean Boiled Wild Dandelion Greens with Garlic Lemon Oil (Radika)
description: Purist Aegean wild green meze: freshly foraged wild dandelion greens (radika) flash-boiled in salted water to retain emerald brilliance, bathed in a punchy emulsion of early-harvest olive oil, crushed garlic, and lemon.

ingredients.name: Fresh Wild Dandelion Greens (Radika, washed thoroughly)
ingredients.substitute: Italian dandelion chicory, wild arugula or escarole

steps.instruction: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Plunge radika greens and boil uncovered for 6-8 minutes until tender.
Transfer greens immediately into an ice bath to lock in the vivid green color.
Drain thoroughly and press out excess water; arrange on a serving platter.
Vigorously whisk early-harvest olive oil, fresh lemon juice, and crushed garlic into a cloudy emulsion; pour generously over the warm greens.

titleEn: Stuffed Swiss Chard Rolls with Herbed Rice and Pine Nuts (Pazı Sarması)
description: Velvety, gossamer Swiss chard rolls filled with rice seasoned with sweet caramelized onions, pine nuts, dried currants, mint, and cinnamon, braised slowly in olive oil and lemon.

ingredients.name: Large Swiss Chard Leaves (Pazı, blanched)
ingredients.substitute: Green Swiss chard or large beet greens

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil & Lemon Juice

steps.instruction: Dip Swiss chard leaves in boiling water for 30 seconds; shock in cold water and slice out the thick central stem.
Sauté onions, pine nuts, currants, spices, and rice in olive oil until translucent.
Place a spoonful of filling on each half leaf, tuck sides in, and roll into slender parcels. Arrange snugly in a pot.
Weight with a plate, add 1.25 cups water and olive oil, and simmer covered on low heat until tender. Cool in pot.
